messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the runtime rollout (v2.7.3) the canary cohort is showing a clear p95/p99 regression around 10:20 UTC. p95 went from ~110ms -> ~230ms, p99 jumping to ~760ms. Affected: cohort-rc1 and ACME (enterprise). Dash: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/r/latency/canary?range=15m :rotating_light:

mia: I see same in the heatmap: late tail on the hotpath 'stream' requests. Traces show long waits inside the kernel-scheduler step and occasional KV cache misses. Example trace id: trace-abc123.

jon: Quick metric check: KV cache miss rate + batching latency both increased at rollout time. Also note we flipped the quantization knob for some model variants in this release (quant-opt enabled by default). Could be related to serialization or slower kernels for certain shapes.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2.7.3 -> completed for cohort-rc1 at 1798456680.

devon: Hypothesis list: 1) kernel scheduler change causing contention on hotpath; 2) quantized kernel path slower for these batch shapes; 3) increased cold KV-cache misses due to new model variant mapping. Proposed immediate mitigations: rollback canary -> v2.7.2 for affected cohorts, or enable runtime fallback to legacy model-variant for ACME; reduce batch size to 4 for the hotpath; prewarm KV cache; disable quant-opt flag for quick test. Also propose a bisect between v2.7.2 and v2.7.3.

mia: Repro steps I'm running now:
```
# sample reproduce with synthetic stream workload
loadgen --target cohort-rc1 --qps 50 --payload templates/stream-short.json --duration 10m
# capture p95/p99 to local file
```
I'll also kick off a KV prewarm: `python tools/prewarm_kv.py --tenants cohort-rc1 --warm 2000`

jon: For bisect we can do traffic split experiment: `rbisect run --left v2.7.2 --right v2.7.3 --metric p99 --traffic 20/80 --duration 20m` — start low traffic then raise. Also when you rollback, confirm `kernel_selector.enabled=false` in cluster config; last rollback missed that flag and left the new scheduler on.

alex: Support ticket created for ACME: SUP-4823. Recommend immediate rollback for ACME and cohort-rc1, plus a temporary routing policy to fallback to model-variant-legacy for business-critical routes. Who can execute rollback now?

mia: I can roll back the canary cohort and run the prewarm. Starting rollback now. Command I use: `rctl rollout rollback --cluster canary --to v2.7.2 --cohort cohort-rc1`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated by mia at 1798456820.

mia: Rollback finished at 1798456900. Early telemetry: cohort-rc1 p95 -> 120ms, p99 -> 310ms. ACME sampling shows similar improvement. Still monitoring 15m window.

devon: Good. Next steps:
- Pause further canary rollouts until root cause confirmed.
- Run bisect overnight with traffic ramp to 50/50 and collect stack/trace samples.
- Jon to run kernel-selector sim against synthetic workloads (small batch / streaming shapes).
- I'll draft a short postmortem and remediation plan (quant flag gating, add kvcache prewarm to rollout job).

jon: I'll also run a kernel micro-benchmark across quant/non-quant kernels and different seq-len/batch shapes and upload results to the experiment board. If quant path is slower, we should gate it behind telemetry heatmaps.

support: Notifying ACME: "We've observed a regresssion during a canary runtime rollout; we've rolled back your traffic to the previous runtime and are monitoring. We'll follow up with a timeline and postmortem."

alex: For record: SLOs are p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms. We breached those for the canary cohort; rollback restored SLO for now. Keep canary paused and bisect. After bisect, if root cause is kernel-scheduler, we may need a small patch + targeted rollout with extra telemetry.

ops-bot: action items logged: #A-9872 (rollback), #A-9873 (bisect job), #A-9874 (kselector sim).

mia: Monitoring shows stabilization at 1798456960. Will keep a 1h watch and report back in 30m. :white_check_mark:
